newsitem.title: USA: Florida professor 'driven by pedophilia' - judge.
newsitem.headline: Florida professor 'driven by pedophilia' - judge.

text.p: A Florida university professor charged with illegally bringing a 17-year-old Honduran boy to the United States was denied bond on Monday because he was allegedly "driven by pedophilia."
U.S. Magistrate Ann Vitunac ordered Florida Atlantic University professor Marvin Hersh held in jail until his trial after prosecutors alleged he had sex with the boy.

Hersh, 57, had been under investigation for more than a year when he was charged last week with obtaining a false birth certificate in order to get a U.S. passport to bring the boy to Florida. Prosecutors on Monday filed an additional charge of engaging in sexual activity with a minor under 18, alleging Hersh had sex with the boy he had taken into his home.
"The court determines the defendant is driven by pedophilia and has been continuing this pattern for 15 years," the magistrate said.

Hersh's lawyer, Charles Jaffe, argued that Hersh posed a danger to young boys only when he was abroad. But Vitunac said: "U.S. laws are designed to protect children of any country, not just the United States.

The sex charge, which carries a potential 10-year prison sentence and a $250,000 fine, was added to a series of charges filed last week against Hersh, who is on paid leave from the Boca Raton, Florida-based university.

The government last week said documents found in a suitcase in Hersh's home, which explained how to obtain and use false documents to flee the country and a map of areas where a pedophile could find young boys, proved he was a risk to flee and a danger to the community.

At last week's hearing, Vitunac gave prosecutors until Monday to determine whether Hersh's fingerprints were on the documents, indicating the original charges against him were not enough to keep him in jail if he could not be linked to the documents.
Assistant U.S. Attorney Karen Atkinson on Monday said Hersh's fingerprints were not found, but she gave Vitunac a second complaint alleging that Hersh had sex with the boy he brought to Florida.

Atkinson said the United States had proof Hersh began seeing the youth in Honduras four or five years before he brought him to Florida in 1995. The boy currently is in the care of Florida's Child Welfare Department.
